_comment: Amazon - a MARKETPLACE feed, and a THIRD schema on purpose. It disagrees with both of the feeds we already speak. PackHub's direct JSON gives us a number for the price; this one gives us the string a shopper sees, currency symbol and Indian comma grouping included ('Rs 1,14,900'). BoxBazaar's CSV gives us a bare shipping range; this one buries the range in a sentence that also names the warehouse. PackHub gives a clean list of specs and BoxBazaar a pipe-separated blob; this one gives a KEY-VALUE SHEET, so the adapter has to take the values and drop the marketing labels. And the price/stock history is keyed BY DATE instead of being a list of objects or a flat trail string. Five different conversions, none of which existed before this file.
_titles_note: The titles are deliberately as messy as the real thing - pack sizes, model codes, warehouse notes and marketing words all crammed into one line. Note that we never parse a title. The gate reads spec_sheet, which is the structured field. AMZ-LAP-1101's title advertises '8GB DDR4' and a buyer skimming would miss it; the spec sheet says 8GB RAM and stage 3 rejects it against a 16GB brief without ever reading the headline.
_delivery_note: Every estimate is quoted to a Chennai 600001 buyer, which is why the same product is 2-3 days from a Chennai hub and 13-14 days from Delhi NCR. The hub is in the text so a judge can see WHY the number differs; only the number survives normalisation, because the number is the only part the delivery gate can use.
_history_note: price_points and stock_points are AUTHORED DEMO DATA, not observations of a real market, and the UI labels them 'simulated market data' wherever they are drawn. A marketplace publishes a shorter window than a contract vendor, so these carry three readings where PackHub carries five - stage 4.5 handles both because it computes over a series, not over a fixed number of points. The last reading of each series must equal the listing's current price_display / in_stock; a feed that contradicts itself would make every signal meaningless.
_reviews_note: top_reviews are shown to the human and read by nothing that decides anything. See agent/models.py, ReviewSnippet: review TEXT is unstructured, adversarial and unreproducible, so it never touches a score. The star RATING does, because it is already a number published the same way for every listing.
